newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises 60 bps to 12 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises 60 bps to 12 pct.

text.p: Croatian average lending rate rose another 60 basis points to 12 percent on Thursday despite weak demand due to high cost of term lending, dealers said.
Daily settlements fetched just 22.8 million kuna against an offer of 60 million.
Most of the 18.8 million fresh trade were interbank call money loans, granted at a steady rate of 10.5 percent.
Term loans were granted at 15 and 16 percent.
Insurers rolled over previous short-term loans at nine percent. Banks renewed one-month deals at 16 percent and charged 17 percent to savings banks.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Friday weaker at 6.1439 against the dollar and firmer at 3.5758 against the German mark.
